01.name: DTC Monitor Status
01.whatIsIt: Internal ECU indicator that informs whether the Check Engine Light (MIL) is illuminated and the total number of fault codes stored.
01.function: Immediately report the injection alert status on the dashboard and the total diagnosed faults.
01.impact: Used for quick vehicle inspections and initial diagnosis of codes stored in memory.

03.name: Fuel System Status
03.whatIsIt: Operational state of the air/fuel mixture control strategy (Open Loop or Closed Loop).
03.function: Indicate whether the ECU is adjusting fuel injection in real-time based on oxygen sensor readings.
03.impact: In Open Loop (cold engine or full throttle), the ECU uses fixed maps; in Closed Loop, it targets the ideal stoichiometric ratio.

04.name: Calculated Engine Load
04.whatIsIt: Percentage of current engine airflow relative to theoretical maximum airflow at the same RPM.
04.function: Indicate the theoretical percentage of engine torque currently being requested.
04.impact: Used by the ECU to determine fuel injection quantity and ignition spark advance.

05.name: Engine Coolant Temperature (ECT)
05.whatIsIt: Thermistor located in the engine block, cylinder head, or thermostat housing.
05.function: Measure the temperature of the coolant fluid circulating to cool the engine.
05.impact: Critical parameter for cold-start fuel enrichment, ignition timing adjustment, and cooling fan activation.

06.name: Short Term Fuel Trim (Bank 1)
06.whatIsIt: Dynamic and instantaneous injection time correction based on immediate oxygen sensor feedback.
06.function: Compensate for momentary mixture variations to maintain the stoichiometric ratio.
06.impact: Positive values add fuel (lean mixture); negative values reduce fuel (rich mixture).

07.name: Long Term Fuel Trim (Bank 1)
07.whatIsIt: Long-term adaptive memory accumulated by the ECU to correct constant mixture deviations.
07.function: Compensate for systematic deviations, such as fuel injector wear or small vacuum leaks.
07.impact: Variations beyond ±10% to ±15% indicate vacuum leaks, contaminated fuel, or fuel delivery issues.

08.name: Short Term Fuel Trim (Bank 2)
08.whatIsIt: Instantaneous injection time correction for the second cylinder bank in V6, V8, or Boxer engines.
08.function: Maintain balanced air/fuel mixture in the engine's secondary bank.
08.impact: Allows comparing injection response between both sides of the engine in dual-bank configurations.

09.name: Long Term Fuel Trim (Bank 2)
09.whatIsIt: Long-term accumulated adaptive memory for the mixture in the second cylinder bank.
09.function: Permanently adjust Bank 2 injection to compensate for component wear.
09.impact: Significant differences compared to Bank 1 point to specific issues in one of the banks.

0A.name: Fuel Rail Pressure (Pump)
0A.whatIsIt: Reading from the pressure sensor installed in the low-pressure fuel supply line.
0A.function: Monitor supply pressure delivered by the fuel pump to the fuel rail.
0A.impact: Pressures below specification cause misfires and lean mixture; high pressures cause fuel excess.

0B.name: Intake Manifold Absolute Pressure (MAP)
0B.whatIsIt: Piezoresistive sensor measuring absolute pressure inside the intake manifold.
0B.function: Report vacuum level in naturally aspirated engines or boost pressure in turbocharged engines.
0B.impact: Essential parameter in the Speed-Density method to calculate intake air mass and fuel injection.

0C.name: Engine Speed (RPM)
0C.whatIsIt: Signal generated by the crankshaft position sensor (CKP).
0C.impact: Fundamental data for injection timing, ignition spark firing, and torque calculation.

0D.name: Vehicle Speed
0D.whatIsIt: Signal from the vehicle speed sensor (VSS) located on the gearbox or coming from the ABS module.
0D.function: Report the actual travel speed of the vehicle in km/h.
0D.impact: Used for cruise control, traction control, and deceleration fuel cut-off (Cut-off).

0E.name: Ignition Timing Advance
0E.whatIsIt: Spark timing angle relative to Top Dead Center (TDC) of the piston.
0E.function: Report when the spark plug fires during the compression stroke.
0E.impact: Optimized ignition timing delivers maximum mechanical efficiency; excessive advance causes knocking (pinging).

0F.name: Intake Air Temperature (IAT)
0F.whatIsIt: Thermistor located in the intake duct or integrated into the MAF sensor.
0F.function: Measure the temperature of fresh air entering the intake system.
0F.impact: Since cold air is denser, the ECU uses this data to calculate actual air mass and adjust fuel density.

10.name: Air Flow Rate (MAF)
10.whatIsIt: Hot-wire or hot-film sensor located in the air filter duct.
10.function: Directly measure the amount of air entering the engine in grams per second (g/s).
10.impact: Enables precise calculation of fuel required to maintain the stoichiometric mixture.

11.name: Throttle Position (TPS)
11.whatIsIt: Potentiometric or Hall-effect sensor installed on the throttle body.
11.function: Indicate the opening percentage of the intake throttle plate.
11.impact: Informs the ECU of driver intent (idle, rapid acceleration, or wide-open throttle).

13.name: Oxygen Sensors Present
13.whatIsIt: Bitmask indicating the number and location of oxygen sensors in the vehicle.
13.function: Map the presence of pre- and post-catalyst sensors in the exhaust system.
13.impact: Instructs the scanner on which oxygen sensor positions should be queried.

14.name: Oxygen Sensor Voltage (B1S1)
14.whatIsIt: Primary oxygen sensor for Bank 1, located in the manifold before the catalytic converter.
14.function: Generate a voltage signal (0.1V to 0.9V) proportional to residual exhaust oxygen.
14.impact: Primary signal used by the ECU to adjust closed-loop air/fuel mixture.

15.name: Oxygen Sensor Voltage (B1S2)
15.whatIsIt: Secondary oxygen sensor for Bank 1, located downstream of the catalytic converter.
15.function: Monitor oxygen storage capacity of the catalytic converter.
15.impact: A stable voltage between 0.6V and 0.8V indicates a healthy catalyst; frequent fluctuations indicate degradation.

16.name: Oxygen Sensor Voltage (B2S1)
16.whatIsIt: Primary pre-catalyst oxygen sensor for Bank 2 in V-type or Boxer engines.
16.function: Measure exhaust gases from the second cylinder bank.
16.impact: Enables independent air/fuel mixture control for Bank 2.

17.name: Oxygen Sensor Voltage (B2S2)
17.whatIsIt: Secondary post-catalyst oxygen sensor for Bank 2.
17.function: Monitor catalytic conversion efficiency for Bank 2.
17.impact: Used by the ECU to evaluate second-bank catalytic converter operation.

1C.name: OBD Standards Conformity
1C.whatIsIt: Regulatory specification code to which the ECU diagnostic system complies.
1C.function: Identify the regional diagnostic standard (OBD-II, EOBD, JOBD, OBDBr, etc.).
1C.impact: Ensures proper interpretation of communication protocols and environmental tests.

valueMap.15: OBD, OBD II, EOBD, and KOBD
valueMap.23: Heavy Duty Euro OBD Stage I without NOx control (HD EOBD-I)
valueMap.24: Heavy Duty Euro OBD Stage I with NOx control (HD EOBD-I N)
valueMap.25: Heavy Duty Euro OBD Stage II without NOx control (HD EOBD-II)
valueMap.26: Heavy Duty Euro OBD Stage II with NOx control (HD EOBD-II N)
valueMap.33: Heavy Duty Euro OBD Stage VI (HD EOBD-VI)

1F.name: Engine Run Time
1F.whatIsIt: Timer in seconds since the engine was successfully started.
1F.function: Measure continuous engine operation duration during the current trip.
1F.impact: Used by the ECU to enable evaporative diagnostic tests or component warmup procedures.

21.name: Distance Traveled with MIL On
21.whatIsIt: Accumulated mileage traveled by the vehicle while the Check Engine light remained illuminated.
21.function: Record how far the vehicle was driven without resolving detected faults.
21.impact: Indicates duration of operation under fault conditions and fault severity.

22.name: Fuel Rail Pressure (Relative)
22.whatIsIt: Fuel rail pressure measured relative to intake manifold vacuum.
22.function: Monitor differential pressure acting across fuel injectors.
22.impact: Ensures exact fuel delivery regardless of manifold vacuum level.

23.name: Fuel Rail Pressure (Absolute)
23.whatIsIt: Total pressure measured in the fuel rail relative to absolute vacuum.
23.function: Measure injection pressure in Direct Injection (GDI) or Diesel (Common Rail) systems.
23.impact: Essential in high-pressure systems to ensure proper fuel atomization.

2C.name: Commanded EGR
2C.whatIsIt: Percentage opening requested by the ECU for the Exhaust Gas Recirculation (EGR) valve.
2C.function: Regulate exhaust gas volume recirculated into the intake.
2C.impact: Lowers combustion temperature inside cylinders, drastically reducing NOx emissions.

2D.name: EGR Error
2D.whatIsIt: Percentage difference between target EGR position and actual position reported by the sensor.
2D.function: Detect mechanical or electrical operational deviations in the EGR valve.
2D.impact: High values indicate a stuck valve, carbon buildup clogging, or electrical fault.

2E.name: Commanded Evaporative Purge
2E.whatIsIt: Duty cycle percentage applied to the canister purge valve.
2E.function: Control entry of fuel vapors accumulated in the charcoal canister into the manifold.
2E.impact: Recycles fuel tank vapors, preventing evaporative emissions.

2F.name: Fuel Tank Level Input
2F.whatIsIt: Signal sent to the ECU from the fuel tank float sensor.
2F.function: Report remaining fuel percentage in the tank.
2F.impact: Used by the ECU to permit EVAP leak tests, which typically require fuel levels between 15% and 85%.

30.name: Number of Warm-ups Since Codes Cleared
30.whatIsIt: Numeric count of how many times ECU fault memory has been cleared via scanner.
30.function: Maintain a history of fault code clearing interventions.
30.impact: Useful for auditing frequent memory resets performed without physical repairs.

31.name: Distance Traveled Since Codes Cleared
31.whatIsIt: Distance traveled by the vehicle after the last fault memory clear command.
31.function: Evaluate if the vehicle was driven far enough for the ECU to complete self-tests.
31.impact: Indicates whether OBD2 readiness monitors had sufficient time to evaluate systems.

32.name: Evaporative System Vapor Pressure
32.whatIsIt: Ultra-sensitive sensor measuring small pressure or vacuum variations in the fuel vapor line.
32.function: Monitor piping and tank tightness during EVAP leak testing.
32.impact: Detects micro-leaks in the fuel storage system.

33.name: Absolute Barometric Pressure
33.whatIsIt: Piezoelectric sensor measuring local ambient atmospheric pressure.
33.function: Report altitude or ambient air density where the vehicle is operating.
33.impact: Allows air/fuel mixture compensation and turbo boost limiting at high altitudes.

34.name: Oxygen Sensor 1 (B1S1) - Equivalence Ratio
34.whatIsIt: Lambda ratio (λ) measurement provided by a wideband oxygen sensor in Bank 1.
34.function: Indicate precise air/fuel mixture ratio in the exhaust stream.
34.impact: Enables instant, highly accurate mixture corrections.

35.name: Oxygen Sensor 2 (B1S2) - Equivalence Ratio
35.whatIsIt: Lambda ratio (λ) measured by wideband sensor downstream of Bank 1 catalyst.
35.function: Monitor composition of gases exiting the catalytic converter.
35.impact: Used by ECU to evaluate catalyst chemical efficiency.

3C.name: Catalyst Temperature (Bank 1, Sensor 1)
3C.whatIsIt: Measured or estimated temperature at the inlet of Bank 1 primary catalyst.
3C.function: Monitor operational temperature of catalytic chemical conversion elements.
3C.impact: Normal temperatures range from 400°C to 800°C. Values above 950°C cause ceramic substrate melting.

3D.name: Catalyst Temperature (Bank 2, Sensor 1)
3D.whatIsIt: Temperature of Bank 2 primary catalytic element.
3D.function: Monitor thermal reaction in secondary bank manifold.
3D.impact: Prevents structural catalyst damage caused by unburned fuel from misfires.

3E.name: Catalyst Temperature (Bank 1, Sensor 2)
3E.whatIsIt: Temperature measured at secondary stage or outlet of Bank 1 catalyst.
3E.function: Evaluate heat dissipation in secondary exhaust line.
3E.impact: Assists in emissions control and catalyst health diagnosis.

3F.name: Catalyst Temperature (Bank 2, Sensor 2)
3F.whatIsIt: Temperature recorded at secondary catalytic element of Bank 2.
3F.impact: Ensures extended exhaust filtration integrity and efficiency.

41.name: Monitor Status (Current Drive Cycle)
41.whatIsIt: Summary of emission monitor status during active drive cycle.
41.function: Report if all continuous tests have run since last start.
41.impact: Used to verify vehicle readiness for inspection emission testing.

42.name: Control Module Voltage (ECU / Battery)
42.whatIsIt: Electrical voltage supplied by battery and alternator to ECU power pins.
42.function: Monitor main engine electrical system health.
42.impact: Voltages below 12V during cranking cause communication faults and false error codes.

43.name: Absolute Load Value
43.whatIsIt: Normalized, corrected volumetric efficiency of air inducted by cylinders.
43.function: Indicate cylinder air filling independent of altitude or temperature.
43.impact: Used for torque calculation in turbocharged engines and advanced management systems.

44.name: Air/Fuel Equivalence Ratio
44.whatIsIt: Ratio between measured air/fuel ratio and ideal fuel stoichiometry.
44.function: Display global Lambda value in real time.
44.impact: 1.0 represents ideal mixture. Less than 1.0 is rich; greater than 1.0 is lean.

45.name: Relative Throttle Position
45.whatIsIt: Effective percentage throttle opening excluding idle stop position.
45.function: Show effective acceleration input requested from electronic throttle body.
45.impact: Provides precise throttle pedal response sensitivity.

46.name: Ambient Air Temperature
46.whatIsIt: Temperature sensor located on bumper, side mirror, or front grille.
46.function: Report outside air temperature surrounding the vehicle.
46.impact: Used for A/C strategies, trip computer, and cold-start parameters.

47.name: Absolute Throttle Position B
47.whatIsIt: Electrical signal from second potentiometer track (Track B) of electronic throttle body.
47.function: Provide redundant signal for acceleration safety verification.
47.impact: If discrepancy occurs between tracks A and B, ECU enters reduced power limp mode.

48.name: Absolute Throttle Position C
48.whatIsIt: Signal from third position sensor track in high-redundancy throttle bodies.
48.function: Ensure fault tolerance in safety-critical accelerator systems.
48.impact: Prevents unintended acceleration in case of track failures.

49.name: Accelerator Pedal Position D
49.whatIsIt: Signal from first sensor circuit (Track D) of accelerator pedal assembly.
49.impact: Transmits driver torque demand for electronic throttle control.

4A.name: Accelerator Pedal Position E
4A.whatIsIt: Signal from second circuit (Track E) integrated into accelerator pedal.
4A.function: Validate readings from pedal Track D.
4A.impact: Ensures safe pedal operation without unintended throttle runaway.

4B.name: Accelerator Pedal Position F
4B.whatIsIt: Redundant signal from third accelerator pedal circuit.
4B.function: Provide triple-checking on electronic accelerator pedals.

4C.name: Commanded Throttle Actuator
4C.whatIsIt: Percentage current/duty cycle applied to throttle DC motor.
4C.function: Report force exerted by ECU to hold throttle plate at target opening.
4C.impact: High effort at idle indicates dirt buildup obstruction or mechanical binding.

4D.name: Engine Run Time with MIL On
4D.whatIsIt: Accumulated minutes running with Check Engine light illuminated.
4D.function: Measure engine operating duration under active fault conditions.
4D.impact: Used to verify fault persistence and driver neglect duration.

4E.name: Time Since Trouble Codes Cleared
4E.whatIsIt: Total engine run time in minutes since last ECU fault memory clear.
4E.impact: Ensures vehicle was driven sufficiently to validate diagnostic monitors.

51.name: Fuel Type
51.whatIsIt: Identification code for fuel type configured or recognized by ECU.
51.function: Report whether fuel is Gasoline, Ethanol, Diesel, Flex, NGV, or Electric.
51.impact: Adjusts ignition advance, injection timing, and emissions logic.

valueMap.16: Bifuel running electric and combustion engine
valueMap.21: Hybrid running electric and combustion engine

52.name: Ethanol Fuel Percentage
52.whatIsIt: Estimated percentage of alcohol present in fuel tank.
52.function: Display alcohol ratio (0% to 100%) in Flex-Fuel engines.
52.impact: Adjusts injection maps and ignition timing according to blend.

53.name: Absolute EVAP System Vapor Pressure
53.whatIsIt: Extended absolute pressure reading in fuel tank vapor line.
53.function: Measure vapor retention in sealed and pressurized tanks.
53.impact: Prevents evaporative hydrocarbon emissions in modern vehicles.

59.name: Fuel Rail Absolute Pressure
59.whatIsIt: High-resolution total pressure measured in fuel rail.
59.function: Monitor high-pressure direct injection fuel systems.
59.impact: Ensures ideal pressure for proper cylinder fuel atomization.

5A.name: Relative Accelerator Pedal Position
5A.whatIsIt: Effective percentage accelerator pedal opening excluding freeplay.
5A.function: Measure immediate acceleration demand commanded by driver.
5A.impact: Command input for acceleration strategies and transmission shift points.

5B.name: Hybrid Battery Pack Remaining Life
5B.whatIsIt: Percentage of traction battery State of Health (SOH%).
5B.function: Report high-voltage battery health and degradation in hybrid/EVs.
5B.impact: Determines when battery cell balancing or replacement is required.

5C.name: Engine Oil Temperature
5C.whatIsIt: Thermal sensor in oil pan, gallery, or filter housing.
5C.impact: Oil operates ideally between 80°C and 110°C; temperatures above 125°C degrade viscosity and protective film.

5D.name: Fuel Injection Timing
5D.whatIsIt: Crankshaft angle relative to TDC where fuel injection begins.
5D.function: Synchronize injection timing in Diesel or Direct Injection engines.
5D.impact: Improves combustion efficiency, reduces noise, and minimizes soot.

5E.name: Engine Fuel Rate
5E.whatIsIt: Instantaneous fuel flow consumed by engine in liters per hour.
5E.impact: Serves as baseline for calculating average fuel economy and range.

5F.name: Emission Requirements Designed For
5F.whatIsIt: Code specifying environmental control legislation adopted by ECU.
5F.impact: Defines fault thresholds required to illuminate Check Engine light.

61.name: Driver's Demanded Engine Torque
61.whatIsIt: Percentage torque level requested by accelerator pedal position.
61.function: Convert pedal input into target engine torque requirement.
61.impact: Baseline calculation for throttle opening, turbo boost, and gear shifts.

62.name: Actual Engine Torque
62.whatIsIt: Estimated percentage torque produced by engine at crankshaft.
62.function: Report current mechanical output force generated by combustion.
62.impact: Used by automatic transmission modules and stability control (ESP).

63.name: Engine Reference Torque
63.whatIsIt: Constant nominal maximum torque rating of engine in Newton-meters (Nm).
63.function: Provide physical scale in Nm to convert percentage torque values.
63.impact: Allows scanner to convert percentage torque into actual Newton-meters.

66.name: Mass Air Flow Sensor A
66.whatIsIt: Extended range air flow sensor on primary intake duct A.
66.function: Measure high airflow rates in performance or dual-intake engines.
66.impact: Improves fuel calculation accuracy in large or twin-turbo engines.

67.name: Engine Coolant Temp. (Multiple Sensors)
67.whatIsIt: Combined thermal readings at engine outlet and radiator.
67.function: Monitor coolant temperature differential across radiator.
67.impact: Enables diagnosis of stuck thermostat valves and radiator inefficiency.

68.name: Intake Air Temp. (Multiple Sensors)
68.whatIsIt: Thermal sensors installed before and after charge air cooler (Intercooler).
68.function: Evaluate cooling efficiency of turbo boosted air.
68.impact: Protects against improper air density in combustion chamber.

6F.name: Turbocharger Inlet Pressure
6F.whatIsIt: Pressure sensor located at turbocompressor air inlet.
6F.function: Measure air filter restriction or compressor inlet pressure.
6F.impact: Identifies clogged air filters and pressure drops at turbo intake.

78.name: Exhaust Gas Temp. (EGT) - Bank 1
78.whatIsIt: Exhaust stream temperature measurement across up to 4 sensors in Bank 1.
78.function: Measure real-time exhaust gas temperature for Bank 1.
78.impact: Protects turbochargers and catalytic converters/filters from thermal destruction.

79.name: Exhaust Gas Temp. (EGT) - Bank 2
79.whatIsIt: Exhaust stream temperature measurement across up to 4 sensors in secondary Bank 2.
79.function: Monitor exhaust temperature for the second cylinder bank in V or Boxer engines.
79.impact: Ensures thermal shock protection and bank-to-bank balance.

81.name: Engine Run Time for Emissions Control
81.whatIsIt: Accumulated minutes with engine operating under clean emission controls.
81.function: Record duration of eco-friendly operation in current cycle.
81.impact: Used to validate compliance with environmental norms.

82.name: Time Since Engine Start for Emission Control
82.whatIsIt: Elapsed minutes since catalysts/filters reached operating temperature.
82.function: Evaluate time required for aftertreatment to reach full efficiency.
82.impact: Analyzes warmup speed of sensors and catalysts.

83.name: EVAP System Vapor Pressure (Alt)
83.whatIsIt: Alternative fuel tank vapor pressure measurement channel in Pascals (Pa).
83.function: Measure tank pressure changes for leak testing.
83.impact: Enables precise leak detection in modern EVAP systems.

84.name: Fuel Injection Timing / Advance
84.whatIsIt: Crankshaft angle where injection pulse starts relative to TDC.
84.function: Synchronize injector firing with intake/compression stroke.
84.impact: Prevents fuel wetting on cold cylinder walls and reduces soot.

85.name: Engine Fuel Rate (Alt)
85.whatIsIt: Alternative continuous consumption measurement channel in L/h.
85.function: Record fuel consumption in high resolution.
85.impact: Used in fleet telemetry and technical fuel logging.

91.name: Engine Oil Temperature (Alt)
91.whatIsIt: Secondary oil temperature sensor in cylinder head gallery.
91.impact: Protects valvetrain against oil film breakdown from extreme heat.

92.name: Fuel Injection Pulse Correction
92.whatIsIt: Compensation applied in microseconds to fuel injection pulse width.
92.function: Adjust mechanical injector opening time based on electrical voltage.
92.impact: Prevents fuel volume variations caused by battery voltage fluctuations.

98.name: NOx Sensor Concentration
98.whatIsIt: Specialized ceramic sensor measuring exhaust nitrogen oxide emissions.
98.function: Measure NOx pollutant concentration in parts per million (ppm).
98.impact: Determines required reductant fluid (DEF / AdBlue) injection quantity.

A1.name: Fuel Injection Data (Rate & Timing)
A1.whatIsIt: Combined flow rate and pulse width signal from fuel system.
A1.impact: Allows evaluation of fuel injector wear and delivery drift.

A2.name: Cylinder Fuel Rate
A2.whatIsIt: Fuel mass metered per cycle individually for each cylinder.
A2.impact: Detects uncalibrated or clogged injectors causing engine vibration.

A3.name: Engine Friction Torque
A3.whatIsIt: Calculated torque loss caused by internal friction of moving parts.
A3.function: Report internal resistance engine must overcome to rotate.
A3.impact: Sudden increases indicate wrong lubricant, worn bearings, or excessive accessory drag.

A4.name: Exhaust Gas Routing Temperature
A4.whatIsIt: Temperature measured in exhaust gas bypass duct.
A4.function: Regulate gas flow temperature to preheat catalysts or turbine.
A4.impact: Speeds up exhaust system light-off and prevents turbo thermal shock.

A6.name: Odometer (ECU Mileage)
A6.whatIsIt: Actual mileage stored in non-volatile engine ECU memory.
A6.function: Store total distance traveled by vehicle.
A6.impact: Essential for verifying odometer accuracy indicated on instrument cluster.

A7.name: NOx Sensor (Bank 1)
A7.whatIsIt: Sensor measuring nitrogen oxides in Bank 1 exhaust line.
A7.function: Evaluate NOx pollutant level produced by Bank 1.
A7.impact: Adjusts DEF dosing rate or limits torque if NOx levels exceed regulatory limits.

A8.name: NOx Sensor (Bank 2)
A8.whatIsIt: Secondary exhaust NOx sensor for Bank 2.
A8.impact: Ensures environmental compliance on large displacement engines.

AA.name: Charge Air Cooler Temp. (Intercooler)
AA.whatIsIt: Temperature sensor located after turbo charge air cooler.
AA.function: Measure compressed air temperature after cooling.
AA.impact: Cool air increases engine power. If intercooler exceeds 60°C, engine efficiency drops.

AB.name: Injection Rail Pressure
AB.whatIsIt: Fuel rail pressure reading in direct fuel injection systems.
AB.function: Monitor high pressure required for direct injectors.
AB.impact: Faults cause immediate engine stumbling, acceleration hesitation, or stalling.

AF.name: Secondary Air System Control
AF.whatIsIt: Operating percentage of electric secondary air pump.
AF.function: Inject fresh air into exhaust manifold during cold starts.
AF.impact: Promotes reaction with unburned fuel, rapidly heating catalyst within seconds.

B4.name: Oxygen Sensor Temperature (B1, B2)
B4.whatIsIt: Ceramic temperature of oxygen sensors in Bank 1 and Bank 2.
B4.function: Ensure sensors reach active operating range (above 350°C).
B4.impact: Adjusts power to sensor electric heaters to prevent thermal shock damage.

C4.name: EGR Valve Control (Advanced)
C4.whatIsIt: Command signal and extended position of EGR recirculation valve.
C4.function: Precisely adjust recirculated exhaust gas rate.
C4.impact: Maximizes emission reduction without destabilizing engine idle.

C5.name: Variable Geometry Turbo Control (VGT)
C5.whatIsIt: Actuation percentage of Variable Geometry Turbocharger (VGT) vanes.
C5.function: Regulate angle of internal turbocompressor vanes.
C5.impact: Ensures instant boost at low RPM while preventing dangerous overboost spikes.

C6.name: Diesel Particulate Filter Pressure (DPF)
C6.whatIsIt: Differential pressure sensor measuring restriction across DPF filter.
C6.function: Measure soot saturation accumulated inside particulate filter.
C6.impact: High differential pressure indicates clogged filter, triggering DPF regeneration.

C8.name: Injector Learning Time
C8.whatIsIt: Time in milliseconds ($ms$) for injector micro-shot learning calculation.
C8.function: Self-correct injection pulse width due to mechanical nozzle wear.
C8.impact: Eliminates injector clatter and guarantees smooth, quiet engine idling.

CB.name: NOx Sensor (Post-Catalyst)
CB.whatIsIt: NOx measurement at exhaust outlet downstream of SCR system.
CB.function: Confirm SCR catalyst reduced NOx contamination.
CB.impact: Validates correct DEF / AdBlue dosing operation.

CD.name: Particulate Matter Sensor (PM)
CD.whatIsIt: Exhaust sensor measuring soot concentration in $mg/m^3$.
CD.function: Monitor DPF filter soot retention efficiency.
CD.impact: Detects cracks or pinholes in DPF ceramic filter substrate.

CE.name: Intake Air Heater
CE.whatIsIt: Actuation percentage of intake grid heater element.
CE.function: Warm intake air for cold starting in Diesel engines.
CE.impact: Facilitates cold fuel ignition and eliminates white start-up smoke.

D0.name: Fuel System Pressure (High Pressure)
D0.whatIsIt: High pressure rail reading in Diesel Common Rail or GDI Direct Injection.
D0.function: Measure injection pressure (ranging from 200 to over 2000 bar).
D0.impact: Enables precise fuel metering in milligrams under extreme pressure.

D2.name: Electric Water Pump Control
D2.whatIsIt: Duty cycle signal sent to variable electric coolant pump.
D2.function: Regulate coolant circulation on demand, independent of engine speed.
D2.impact: Promotes rapid warm-up of cold engine and reduces parasitic engine drag.

DF.name: Exhaust Control Status (DPF/NOx)
DF.whatIsIt: Control status of exhaust filter cleaning and regeneration cycles.
DF.function: Inform if ECU is performing DPF filter regeneration.
DF.impact: During regeneration, exhaust reaches elevated temperatures to burn off trapped soot.

E3.name: A/C Compressor Motor Temp.
E3.whatIsIt: Thermal sensor attached to electric A/C compressor motor in Hybrid/EVs.
E3.function: Monitor climate control compressor motor temperature.
E3.impact: Temporarily disables A/C to prevent electric compressor motor burnout.

EA.name: Inverter Temperature (Hybrids)
EA.whatIsIt: Temperature sensor installed on high-voltage power inverter.
EA.function: Monitor heating in EV/Hybrid power semiconductor modules.
EA.impact: Inverter converts battery DC to AC motor power. Overheating limits available drive power.
